report_name: ASCII Smuggling Phishing Attack Evades Filters with Unicode

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used 'ASCII smuggling' by inserting invisible Unicode characters from the Tags block (U+E0000–U+E007F) into financial keywords within phishing emails. This split the words at a code level, allowing emails to bypass keyword-based security filters while appearing normal to the user. The technique was repurposed from AI prompt injection research.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The phishing emails contained links that lured victims with SBA-themed financial offers to a landing page designed to harvest detailed business and financial information.

tools.name: ActiveCampaign
tools.description: The ActiveCampaign marketing platform was used for the distribution of the high-volume phishing emails.

campaigns.name: SBA Loan-Themed ASCII Smuggling Phishing Campaign
campaigns.description: A high-volume phishing campaign that used 'ASCII smuggling' with invisible Unicode characters to bypass email security filters. The campaign sent millions of emails with SBA loan themes to harvest business and financial information.

identities.name: U.S. Small Business Administration
identities.description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) was impersonated in the theme of the phishing campaign, used to lure victims with financial offers.

indicators.name: ASCII Smuggling using Unicode Tags Block
indicators.pattern:
title: Phishing Email with Unicode Tags Block Obfuscation (ASCII Smuggling)
id: 7b9c1d8e-4a3b-4f1e-9c8d-6a5b4c3d2e1f
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of invisible Unicode characters from the Tags block (U+E0000–U+E007F) within an email body. This technique, known as 'ASCII smuggling', is used to bypass keyword-based email security filters. This rule should be applied to raw email content (e.g., EML files).
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/03/ascii-smuggling-crosses-over-from-ai-prompt-injection-to-phishing-evasion/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-06
tags:
  - attack.t1027
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file
detection:
  selection:
    Contents|re: '[\uE0000-\uE007F]'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of invisible Unicode characters from the Tags block (U+E0000–U+E007F) in email content to evade security filters, a technique known as ASCII smuggling.
